subject: alt. to Pareto prior for (a + b) in Beta(a,b) rec. in BDA ch. 5?

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: alt. to Pareto prior for (a + b) in Beta(a,b) rec. in BDA ch. 5?
parts:
Andrew:

I recall you saying at one point that you would now use
something other than the following parameterization for
hierarchical priors a vector of binomial/bernoulli parameters
theta in (0, 1):

phi ~ uniform(0,1) [equivalently, beta(1,1)]

kappa ~ Pareto(epsilon, 1.5) [requires constant epsilon and kappa > epsilon]

theta[k] ~ beta(phi * kappa, (1 - phi) * kappa)

I currently just copied that recommendation from BDA chapter 5
into the Stan manual, but now that we're thinking more about
weakly or even more strongly informative priors, it may be time
to update that advice.

And should we be more informative on phi? Perhaps something
as simple as Beta(2,2) as the default on the grounds that we probably
don't want estimates for theta at the boundary?

- Bob

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] alt. to Pareto prior for (a + b) in Beta(a,b) rec. in BDA ch. 5?
parts:
I added an issue:

https://github.com/stan-dev/stan/issues/1563

Please feel free to edit it to reflect best naming practices.
I tend to think of mu as being unbounded and inherited the tradition
of using theta and phi for probability values or simplexes from machine
learning. But if everyone in stats expects mu for a prior mean parameter,
I'm OK with that.

What do we call the prior count (- 2) parameter?

I added a rider to add symmetric forms of both densities.

- Bob
